scope: Exact existing /uc.js banner loader identity plus six optional documented or SDK-defined query settings.

sources.notes: Script tag data attributes table lists optional dialog type, level, framework, blockingmode and consentmode. Its two-letter culture and IAB-only wording is superseded in part by current language and TCF guides.
Explicitly permits all data-* attributes to be carried on the same loader query without the data- prefix.
Exact query reading, optional/blank fallback, case-insensitive framework aliases, blockingmode and consentmode, and explicit dataredaction warning. Actual unchanged sections replayed offline.
Optional data-culture is available on both banner and declaration; configured language availability remains external.
PT-BR and ZH-HANT are published variants; languages beyond the list may be added. No closed culture grammar is imposed.
Current TCF guide recommends TCF. Its literal data-framework query example conflicts with the actual loader, which reads framework only. No unsupported alias is added.
Explicit EU loader mirrors recorded for a future match-scope option. Matching hosts stay unchanged in this depth pass.
Documented all-zero placeholder source only. Confirms declaration query culture is passed through without a closed value check; no account-specific loader or follow-up request was fetched.

additional_gaps_closed: HTML-only setting gap is closed only for the officially supported query carriers.
limitations: Settings carried only in HTML are not visible in URL artifacts; all new query contracts are optional.
Empty query values are ignored or fall back to attributes by the source, so all six new contracts allow empty values.

The SDK reads the first literal value-bearing query key. The engine checks all submitted decoded pairs. An invalid duplicate may therefore receive advisory feedback although the SDK ignores that occurrence; ordering controls record both cases.
The engine decodes query keys while the SDK matches literal key names. Encoded-name controls document that difference. No claim of identical SDK parsing is made.
Bare query keys are omitted by the preserved legacy extractor and are not treated as populated overrides.
Culture remains open, including PT-BR, ZH-HANT, three-letter/custom strings and future configured variants. Availability and rendering require account context.
Type and level are passed through by the loader. Their findings are advice from the documented setting table, not receiver rejection or proof the SDK blocks unknown strings.
Framework aliases describe the pinned loader, not every future framework. The data-framework query typo in the TCF guide is not treated as a working alias.
No consent lifecycle, legal compliance, account authorization, HTML blocking implementation or declaration rendering contract is inferred.
negative_controls: documented regional and custom culture strings

other_pack_assessments.disposition: No manifest change. Public source passes culture through and cannot justify a safe closed culture rule.
No cfg deepening. New checklist example is Android/cert-host scope and cannot justify universal Browser SDK field rules; conflicting dcrcert example and current closed enum are handed to coordinator.
